summary: Opaque server error surge during long-polling / keepalive handshake under hedged client retries
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-12T08:40 UTC Flowbeam (dedicated tenant) reported sustained 50x+ spike in 5xx responses on several chat and streaming routes. Customers saw long-lived streaming sessions fail with 502/503 and short synchronous requests get 500/502. Impact: multiple production customers experienced failed requests and degraded tail latency; Flowbeam reported user-facing failures in their webhooks and live chat integration.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulated Flowbeam traffic pattern: many long-polling websocket/stream sessions with periodic hedged client retries (mobile SDK default with no jitter). 2) Concurrent embedding and chat requests from same tenant at ~200 concurrent connections. 3) Observe accept-queue growth and intermittent keepalive/handshake timeouts. 4) Retry storm causes multiple upstream worker evictions and GPU watchdog resets.
observed_metrics_and_logs:
- API gateway 5xx rate: rose from 0.4% baseline to 8.7% at peak (08:42-08:55 UTC).
- Runtime upstream restarts: several runtimes logged 'GPU watchdog reset' and 'worker exit: signal 6' aligned with 502 bursts.
- Kernel/tcp stats: accept_queue backlog increased, large number of sockets in FIN_WAIT/UNKNOWN.
- KV cache eviction spikes: eviction rate jumped 5-8x during the window.
- Trace sample: streaming session A: half-closed handshake, client hedged retry fired, gateway retried and created duplicate inflight sessions; runtime dropped thread with memory footprint spike before NVML reset.
- Relevant logs: apigw logs show many 'keepalive handshake timeout' and 'upstream reset while waiting for body'.
hypothesis_and_investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: A hedged-retry pattern from the Flowbeam mobile/web SDK (no jitter) created a tight retry fanout on slow keepalive handshakes. This caused accept-queue pressure at the ingress path, produced duplicate session handoffs to ephemeral proxies, and led to KV cache thrash and elevated GPU memory pressure. Increased GPU memory pressure triggered the runtime GPU watchdog to reset workers, causing 502/503 waves.
Investigation: Support reproduced a reduced version in staging by enabling hedged retries and blocking one runtime's ephemeral proxy handoff. Engineers traced correlation between hedged retry bursts and KV prefetch invalidations. Heap and nvml logs matched GPU watchdog timestamps. Autoscaler was filling backfill workers; during backfill theruntime warmed kernels causing temporary memory fragmentation.
Mitigations tested in staging: 1) Disabled hedged retries at SDK-level for test tenant; 2) Raised accept queue limit and increased keepalive_window on ingress proxies; 3) Applied short-term per-tenant concurrency cap to Flowbeam traffic; 4) Adjusted prefetch window to reduce KV eviction pressure. All mitigations reduced 5xx rate in staging simulation.
actions_taken_and_resolution:
Immediate actions (08:58 UTC): applied per-tenant concurrency cap (soft limit 120) to Flowbeam in us-east and enabled a short-term rate limit on hedged retries at apigw layer. We also increased keepalive timeout from 15s to 30s for the affected host pool to reduce handshake churn. Result: 5xx rate dropped to ~0.6% within 20 minutes and runtime restarts ceased.
Permanent actions (completed next day): rolled out apigw change to add jitter to hedged-retry enforcement and per-tenant hedged-retry guardrails; updated autoscaler warmup to stagger kernel compilation during backfills; changed prefetch/kv cache eviction thresholds to be less aggressive under concurrent long-polling. Noted follow-up: SDK teams (Flowbeam and public mobile SDK) to adopt randomized hedging jitter; product to add tenant-level backpressure SLOs.
Status: Incident resolved; customer confirmed recovery and continued monitoring enabled.
follow_up_items:
- Engineering to implement per-tenant backpressure metrics and alerting (owner: Samir Gupta).
- Product/Solutions to coordinate with Flowbeam to add SDK hedged-retry jitter and recommend connection backoff (owner: Maya Chen).
- Observability: add dashboard for hedged retry fanout and KV eviction correlation (owner: Diego Ramirez).
- Runbook update: include hedged-retry detection and temporary tenant caps in apigw runbook (owner: SRE).
